transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi—thanks for seeing me. I guess what pushed me to come in is… it’s probably not a huge thing, but over the last year or so I’ve noticed I get pulled off what I’m doing really easily. Like a phone buzz, someone walking past my office, or even just some random thought—like something with my in-laws—and suddenly I’m not on the task anymore before I even realize it. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it’s been happening enough that I figured I should ask about it.
Looking back to when you were a child, were you already someone who got distracted easily?

Yeah… I think so, actually. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was a “bad kid” or anything, but teachers did move my seat around a lot. Usually because I was talking too much, or I’d get up without asking, or I’d answer before they were even done asking the question. So… yeah, looking back, there was probably some of that then too.
Do these distraction problems create noticeable difficulties for you at home?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still keeping up overall, so I don’t want to overstate it. But at home, yeah, it does show up. If we’ve made family plans or my wife is counting on me to follow through on something, and I get pulled off track, it can come across like I didn’t care or wasn’t listening.

It’s not like everything is falling apart, but I can tell it’s costing me some trust, if that makes sense. And honestly there’s a similar thing at work sometimes—meetings or mentoring conversations don’t go as smoothly as they should, and people can get a little less patient with me. I don’t know if that answers it the right way, but yeah, it’s noticeable.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, I worry about normal stuff—work, family, whether I’m keeping up with what I said I’d do—but I wouldn’t say it’s, like, constant worry about everything.

Unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean. It’s more that my mind jumps around than that I’m sitting there worrying all day, if that makes sense.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task all the way through, even when you want to?

Yeah… I’d say that happens. Not every single time, but enough that I notice it.

Like, I can start a planning document or sit down with one of my managers and I’m really there for the first few minutes, like I’m locked in. And then pretty soon I’ll realize I missed part of what they were saying, sometimes like… half of it, honestly, and I have to ask them to run it back.

I try to cover it and stay engaged, but yeah, staying with it all the way through can be harder than I’d like.
Do you often interrupt people before they’ve finished speaking?

Yeah… I probably do, more than I’d like to admit. I don’t mean to be rude, but I’ll jump in before someone’s finished because I think I know where they’re going.

Like with my wife, I’ve caught myself jumping into her conversations with her parents, and at work I’ll sometimes finish an employee’s thought before they’re done saying it. I usually think I’m helping or keeping things moving, but I can tell it rubs people the wrong way.

So… yes, I guess that does happen.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have days where I’m frustrated or worn out, sure, but not depressed most days.

I wouldn’t want to overstate it. Overall I’d say my mood is… okay, I guess? Not something I’ve really been worried about.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to stay seated or still when you’re supposed to?

Yeah… I mean, not in a dramatic way, I don’t think. But yes, I do feel that.

When I’m supposed to just sit still, like at a family dinner or a church volunteer meeting, I start feeling like there’s kind of a motor running in me. Like I need to shift around, get up, or at least be doing something with my hands.

I try not to make it obvious, because I know it can look impatient or disrespectful, but it’s hard to just… be still. Does that make sense?
When something is really interesting to you, do you usually find you can focus on it for a long time?

If it’s really interesting, I can focus better, yeah… at least at first. I don’t think I’m hopeless with it or anything.

But even then, it’s not always as steady as I’d like. Like I can start a planning document or sit down with one of my managers and be locked in for the first few minutes, and then pretty soon I realize I missed half of what was said. Then I have to ask them to run it back, which is a little embarrassing.

So I guess… yes and no? Interest helps, but it doesn’t totally fix it.
Have these attention problems ever caused a serious consequence for you, like trouble at work or major conflict at home?

I wouldn’t say it’s been catastrophic or anything like that. I’m still keeping up overall… work is still functioning, home is still functioning.

But, yeah, if I’m being honest, it’s starting to cost me a little. At work, people get frustrated when a meeting goes off track or I don’t follow through the way I meant to, especially in mentoring conversations. I can tell their patience is thinner than it used to be.

And at home, it’s more like trust, I guess. If we’ve made family plans and I miss part of what was agreed on or things don’t go the way they should, it creates tension. Not huge blowups all the time, but enough that I know it’s affecting people.

I don’t know if that counts as “serious,” but it’s not nothing.
Do you have trouble falling asleep?

I don’t know that I’d say I have a big problem with falling asleep. Not consistently, anyway.

Some nights I’m wound up and it takes me a bit to settle, but I’ve kind of always thought that was normal adult life, you know? Work, family, things on my mind. I wouldn’t want to overstate it. If you’re asking whether I’m lying there for hours every night, no, not really.
Before age 12, did these attention or restlessness problems clearly cause trouble for you at school or at home?

Yeah… I mean, looking back, I guess it probably did. I don’t want to make it sound like I was some terrible kid or anything, but teachers were always moving my seat around because I talked too much or got up when I wasn’t supposed to.

And I remember blurting out answers before they even finished the question. At the time it just felt like I was excited or being social, but… yeah, I think it caused enough trouble that teachers had to manage me a lot. Does that answer what you mean?
Do these attention and restlessness problems happen in more than one setting, like both at work and at home?

Yes, I think it does happen in both places. I mean, I’m still managing overall, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But at work, people can get frustrated when meetings or mentoring conversations don’t go the way they should, or I don’t follow through exactly like I meant to. And at home, it shows up with family plans—like if I miss part of what we agreed on, it affects trust a bit.

So… yes, more than one setting. Does that make sense?
Do you often make careless mistakes or overlook details when you’re doing work or other tasks?

I’m not sure I’d say “often,” honestly. I mean, everyone misses things here and there, right?

I try pretty hard to check important stuff, especially at work, because I know details matter. I can’t think of a clear pattern where I’m constantly making careless mistakes. Maybe occasionally, but nothing that really stands out to me. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or activities?

I don’t know that I’d call it a major problem. I mean, I have systems and people around me that help keep things moving, so most of the time it doesn’t look disorganized from the outside.

If you mean like planning out steps or keeping track of everything myself… maybe sometimes that’s harder than I’d like to admit, but I’m not sure it rises to “often.” I can usually get it together when it matters. Does that answer it?
Do you often put off or avoid tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort?

I don’t think I really avoid them, no. I mean, if something needs a lot of focus, I might not exactly look forward to it, but I usually try to get it done.

Maybe I’ll delay a little if it feels tedious, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. I can’t think of a big pattern where I’m constantly putting those things off. Does that sound clear?
Do you often lose or misplace things you need, like your phone, keys, paperwork, or other important items?

Not really, no. I mean, I’ll set my phone down and have to look around for it like anyone does, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly losing important things.

Keys and paperwork, I try to keep in the same places because I don’t want that becoming an issue. So… maybe minor stuff once in a while, but nothing that feels like a real pattern. Is that what you mean?

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports ADHD with persistent symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity beginning in childhood, present across multiple settings, and causing functional impairment. Confirmed inattentive symptoms include being easily distracted and difficulty sustaining attention. Confirmed hyperactive/impulsive symptoms include talking excessively in childhood, leaving seat/getting up when not supposed to, blurting out answers, interrupting others, and subjective restlessness ('motor running'). Symptoms were present before age 12 and continue at home and work. Anxiety and depression were not supported as primary explanations, and the symptom count does not support predominantly inattentive presentation.
